subject: PE & Wellbeing
source: National Curriculum (Physical Education); UK Chief Medical Officers' physical activity guidelines. Drive PE folder reviewed (TSS Long-Term PE Plan: fitness, fair play, leadership, resilience) and adapted to at-home, no-equipment, no-contact lessons.

lessons.title: Travelling and stopping
objectives: Move in different ways around a safe space
Stop and freeze on a signal
Show control and care for others

keywords.def: to move from one place to another
to stop still and hold your body
the room around you to move in
not likely to hurt you or anyone else

starter: Bismillah. Show me your biggest stretch.
Show me how to stand very still.

teach.heading: Safety first
bullets: Clear a space bigger than your arms
Socks or shoes, no slippery floor
Stop if you feel unwell and tell a grown-up
A grown-up is in the room
teach.note: Read this slide aloud every lesson. Parents are asked to confirm their child is well enough to take part and to tell the school about any medical condition (e.g. asthma: inhaler within reach). No contact activities in any TGA online PE lesson.

teach.heading: Moving in different ways
bullets: Walk, march, tiptoe
Hop on one foot, then the other
Gallop like a horse in a small space
teach.note: Model each move on camera. Pupils copy. Keep to the space where they can still see the screen. Ask them to use quiet feet.

teach.heading: Stop and freeze
bullets: When I say freeze, stop still
Hold your body like a statue
Look and listen for the signal
teach.note: Play 'Freeze' with a clap. Praise good stopping, not speed. Misconception: stopping means falling over; show a calm stop.

teach.heading: Animal moves
bullets: Frog jumps on the spot
Bear walk on hands and feet
Wiggle your arms like an elephant trunk
teach.note: Choose gentle animal moves. Check wrist comfort before the bear walk and offer a kneeling option.

teach.heading: Cool down
bullets: Breathe in through the nose
Breathe out slowly
Say Alhamdulillah for a healthy body
teach.note: Lead 3 slow breaths. Link to thankfulness for health.

practice: What do we do when I say freeze?
independent: Travel by tiptoeing, hopping and galloping, then freeze on the signal.
Move like a frog five times, then rest.
exit: Make up a short journey: tiptoe, hop, freeze.
Show a grown-up your best freeze.
homework: What do we do on freeze?
lessons.send: Play 'Freeze' with a family member for two minutes.

lessons.title: Balancing like statues
objectives: Hold a balance for five seconds
starter: Hop on your left foot three times.

teach.heading: Safety first
bullets: Clear space around you
Hold on to a wall or sturdy chair if needed
Wobbles are fine, falling is not
Stop and sit if dizzy
teach.note: Read this slide aloud every lesson. Parents are asked to confirm their child is well enough to take part and to tell the school about any medical condition (e.g. asthma: inhaler within reach). No contact activities in any TGA online PE lesson.

teach.heading: Balancing on one foot
bullets: Stand tall and look at one spot
Lift one foot
Count to five in your head
teach.note: Model. Misconception: balance means not moving at all; small wobbles are normal. Use a fixed point to look at.

teach.heading: Wide and narrow shapes
bullets: Stand like a star: wide
Stand like a pencil: narrow
Which is easier to balance?
teach.note: Discuss: a wide base is steadier. Let pupils try each.

teach.heading: Balance on different parts
bullets: Two feet and one hand
Seat and no feet (V sit)
Knees and one hand
teach.note: Offer easier and harder options. No pressure on wrists. Pupils stop if it hurts.

teach.heading: Gentle stretch
bullets: Reach up high
Touch your toes softly
Hold each stretch for five
teach.note: Stretch only until it feels gentle. Never bounce.

practice: Hold a statue pose for three seconds.
Which is steadier: a wide stance or a narrow stance?
independent: Balance on one foot for five seconds on each side.
Make a balance with three parts of your body on the floor.
exit: Create two balances and hold each for five seconds.
Show them to a grown-up and tell them how you kept steady.
lessons.send: Practise balancing on one foot while brushing your teeth.
